name: Quantum
summary: Quantum circuits in chat: write them in Q text, micro QASM or MicroQiskit and get an IBM-style picture with probabilities and Bloch spheres.
description:
Quantum brings the Quantum Web Lab into chat. Send !qc with a circuit in a code block and the bot answers with a picture in the style of IBM Quantum Composer: the circuit with colour-coded gates, the measured results or exact probabilities, and a 3D Bloch sphere for every qubit.

Write circuits the way you like: Q text (H-X#0-M, one row per qubit), micro QASM (OpenQASM 3 or 2), MicroQiskit (Qiskit-style Python: qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2), qc.h(0), qc.cx(0, 1)), or console lines (h 0, cx 0 1). Or build your own circuit a step at a time: !qc h 0, !qc cx 0 1, !qc run, !qc undo, !qc reset, !qc explain h. Add shots=2000 seed=7 on the first line, text for the results as text (a diagram, bars and Bloch arrows in code blocks), or -> qasm, -> qasm2, -> python, -> q or -> diagram to convert a circuit instead of running it. !qlab sends the whole Quantum Web Lab as a mini app: a touch composer with a Bloch sphere, code in three languages, a console and challenges.

Up to 12 qubits. MicroQiskit code is never run as real Python: a small interpreter reads only circuit code (assignments, for, if, print, MicroQiskit and math), with limits on steps, gates and output. Like Qiskit, qubit 0 is the right-most digit of a result. Fonts are IBM Plex (SIL Open Font License); the fonts and the lab (about 1 MB) are downloaded from this marketplace the first time they're needed. This module runs Python, so it needs Settings → Marketplace → Allow modules with code.
